classification.difficultyReason: Rationalise two binomial denominators separately, then cancel the irrational terms to establish rationality.

content.prompt: Show that $\dfrac{2}{6-3\sqrt{3}}-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}+3}$ is rational by first rationalising each denominator.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{7}{3}$, which is rational.

Rationalising each denominator makes the surd terms cancel.
